objectives: Impact the Moon, measure magnetic field, cosmic rays, and interplanetary plasma.
key_discoveries: First spacecraft to reach escape velocity (11.2 km/s), discovered absence of strong lunar magnetic field, detected solar wind in deep space.

objectives: First spacecraft to reach the surface of the Moon / direct impact.
key_discoveries: FIRST HUMAN-MADE OBJECT TO REACH ANOTHER CELESTIAL BODY. Confirmed no significant lunar magnetic field or radiation belt.

objectives: Fly around the Moon and photograph the previously unobserved lunar far side.
key_discoveries: FIRST IMAGES OF THE FAR SIDE OF THE MOON. Revealed far side is mountainous, densely cratered, and lacks large maria seen on near side.

objectives: Transmit high-resolution close-up television photographs of lunar surface before impacting.
key_discoveries: First US success in lunar exploration; transmitted 4,308 high-resolution photos showing craters down to 1 meter in Mare Cognitum.

objectives: Achieve first survivable soft landing on the Moon and transmit surface panoramas.
key_discoveries: FIRST SUCCESSFUL SOFT LANDING ON ANOTHER CELESTIAL BODY. Proved lunar surface could support spacecraft weight (refuting quicksand dust hypothesis).

objectives: First spacecraft to orbit the Moon, study lunar environment and surface gamma radiation.
key_discoveries: FIRST ARTIFICIAL SATELLITE OF THE MOON. Detected lunar crust basaltic composition via gamma-ray spectroscopy; broadcasted 'The Internationale'.

objectives: Demonstrate closed-loop radar-guided soft landing and assess Apollo landing site conditions.
key_discoveries: First US soft landing on the Moon; transmitted 11,237 photos; proved regolith had bearing strength adequate for Apollo Lunar Module.

objectives: Photograph smooth areas of lunar surface to select Apollo and Surveyor landing sites.
key_discoveries: Photographed 5.2 million km2 of the Moon, including first photograph of Earth taken from lunar orbit ('Earthrise' precursor).
payload: Dual-lens 80mm/610mm Film Camera with Onboard Bimax Processor

mission_type: Crewed Lunar Orbiter (Frank Borman, Jim Lovell, William Anders)
objectives: First crewed spacecraft to leave low Earth orbit, reach the Moon, and orbit it 10 times.
key_discoveries: FIRST HUMANS TO WITNESS AND PHOTOGRAPH EARTHRISE; first crewed lunar orbital operations; Christmas Eve Genesis broadcast.

mission_type: Crewed Lunar Landing (Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, Michael Collins)
objectives: Perform a crewed lunar landing and safely return to Earth; deploy scientific instruments and collect samples.
key_discoveries: FIRST HUMAN LANDING ON THE MOON. Returned 21.55 kg of lunar samples; deployed Passive Seismic Experiment and Laser Ranging Retroreflector.

mission_type: Crewed Lunar Landing (Pete Conrad, Alan Bean, Richard Gordon)
objectives: Pinpoint soft landing on Oceanus Procellarum; retrieve components from Surveyor 3 spacecraft; deploy ALSEP.
key_discoveries: Demonstrated pinpoint landing (183 m from Surveyor 3); returned Surveyor 3 camera parts demonstrating space weathering; returned 34.35 kg samples.

objectives: Perform automated drilling and robotic sample return from Mare Fecunditatis.
key_discoveries: FIRST ROBOTIC RETURN OF EXTRATERRESTRIAL SAMPLES TO EARTH (101 grams of titanium-rich basaltic core).

objectives: Deploy the first autonomous/teleoperated robotic roving vehicle on another planetary body.
key_discoveries: FIRST ROBOTIC ROVER ON ANOTHER WORLD. Traveled 10.54 km over 322 Earth days in Mare Imbrium; returned 20,000+ TV images and 206 high-res panoramas.

mission_type: Crewed Lunar Landing (David Scott, James Irwin, Alfred Worden)
objectives: First 'J-mission' (extended stay, Lunar Roving Vehicle, deep drill, orbital SIM bay).
key_discoveries: Explored Hadley Rille and Apennine Front; discovered 'Genesis Rock' (Sample 15415, 4.1 Ga anorthosite from primordial lunar crust); returned 77.31 kg samples.

mission_type: Crewed Lunar Landing (Gene Cernan, Harrison Schmitt, Ronald Evans)
objectives: Geological exploration of Taurus-Littrow valley; first professional geologist on the Moon (Harrison Schmitt).
key_discoveries: Discovered orange volcanic pyroclastic glass beads at Shorty Crater (proof of explosive lunar volcanism); returned 110.5 kg samples (largest single haul).

objectives: Test lightweight military sensors in deep space; map the Moon at ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared wavelengths.
key_discoveries: First global multispectral albedo and mineralogical maps of the Moon; bistatic radar experiment detected evidence of volatile water ice in Shackleton Crater.

objectives: Global polar orbit mapping of lunar composition, surface magnetic fields, gravity anomalies, and volatile outgassing.
key_discoveries: Neutron spectrometer definitively identified high concentrations of hydrogen (consistent with water ice) in permanently shadowed craters at both lunar poles.

objectives: Three-dimensional topographic atlas of the Moon, chemical and mineralogical mapping, search for water ice.
key_discoveries: NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3) aboard Chandrayaan-1 CONFIRMED WATER/HYDROXYL MOLECULES on the lunar surface, especially at polar latitudes.

objectives: Create highest-resolution 3D topographic model, locate water ice in permanently shadowed regions, characterize radiation.
key_discoveries: LROC imaged Apollo landing sites showing rover wheel tracks and flags; LOLA provided the definitive global elevation grid; LCROSS impact into Cabeus crater proved ~5.6% water ice by mass in the regolith plume.

objectives: First-ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon; study South Pole-Aitken (SPA) basin subsurface mantle materials via Queqiao relay satellite.
key_discoveries: FIRST HISTORIC FAR-SIDE LUNAR LANDING (Von Kármán crater). Yutu-2 ground-penetrating radar probed regolith down to 40 meters; identified low-calcium pyroxene and olivine from deep mantle ejecta.
payload: Advanced Small Analyzer for Neutrals (ASAN / Sweden)
Lunar Lander Neutrons and Dosimetry (LND / Germany)

objectives: Demonstrate end-to-end safe and soft landing near lunar south polar region; operate Pragyan rover in-situ.
key_discoveries: HISTORIC SOFT LANDING AT ~69.37° S (Shiv Shakti Point). Discovered sulfur (S), aluminum, calcium, iron, and titanium via LIBS; measured thermal conductivity gradient of polar regolith (ChaSTE) showing 50°C drop 8 cm below surface.
payload: Vikram Lander: ChaSTE (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment)

objectives: First automated drill and scoop sample collection from the lunar far side (South Pole-Aitken Basin / Apollo crater) and return to Earth.
key_discoveries: FIRST FAR-SIDE LUNAR SAMPLE RETURN IN HUMAN HISTORY. Returned 1,935.3 grams of pristine far-side materials; dated basaltic volcanism on far side to 2.83 Ga; uncovered crustal asymmetry mechanisms.
payload: Far-Side Robotic Drill & Robotic Arm Scoop
NILS (Negative Ions on Lunar Surface / ESA)

objectives: Perform first close-range planetary flyby of Mars and capture images of the surface.
key_discoveries: FIRST SUCCESSFUL MARS FLYBY. Returned 21 black-and-white photos revealing a cratered, Moon-like desert; measured atmospheric surface pressure to be only 4.1 to 7.0 mbar (refuting higher pressure models).

objectives: First spacecraft to orbit another planet; map 70% of Martian surface at 1 km resolution.
key_discoveries: FIRST SPACECRAFT TO ORBIT ANOTHER PLANET. Outwaited global dust storm; discovered Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris (named in its honor), ancient dried riverbeds, and outflow channels indicating past liquid water.

objectives: Deliver descent module and lander to Martian surface during ongoing global dust storm; deploy Prop-M rover.
key_discoveries: FIRST SURVIVABLE SOFT LANDING ON MARS (Ptolemaeus crater, 1971-12-02). Transmitted partial gray television image for 14.5 seconds before communications terminated due to corona discharge or storm winds.

objectives: High-resolution orbital mapping, search for biosignatures/life in Martian regolith, record weather and seismic activity.
key_discoveries: FIRST OPERATIONAL LONG-TERM LANDER ON MARS (Chryse Planitia, operated 2,307 Earth days). Returned first color panoramas; detected no organic molecules in soil via GC-MS; Gas Exchange and Labeled Release biology experiments showed chemical reactions attributed to soil oxidants (perchlorates).
payload: Biology Investigation (Pyrolytic Release, Labeled Release, Gas Exchange)

objectives: Independent validation of Martian biology, atmosphere, surface imagery, and seismology in northern plains.
key_discoveries: Landed in Utopia Planitia; photographed water-ice frost deposition on rocks in northern winter; detected candidate marsquake event with lander seismometer.

objectives: Global high-resolution imaging, topography, mineralogy, gravity field, and magnetic field mapping.
key_discoveries: MOLA laser altimeter provided the benchmark global topography of Mars; discovered ancient magnetic striping in southern highlands (evidence of past dynamo); identified hematite deposits at Meridiani Planum.
payload: MOC (Mars Orbiter Camera - Wide & Narrow Angle)

objectives: Demonstrate low-cost airbag landing system and deploy the first successful mobile rover on Mars.
key_discoveries: FIRST SUCCESSFUL ROVER ON MARS (Sojourner, 10.6 kg). Explored Ares Vallis catastrophic outflow floodplain; analyzed rocks 'Barnacle Bill' and 'Yogi' showing andesitic-to-basaltic composition.
payload: IMP (Imager for Mars Pathfinder - Stereo Mast)
APXS (Alpha Proton X-Ray Spectrometer on Rover)

mission_type: Mars Global Mapping Orbiter & Telecom Relay
objectives: Search for water ice via gamma rays and neutrons; global thermal infrared mineral mapping; primary communications relay.
key_discoveries: LONGEST CONTINUOUSLY OPERATING SPACECRAFT AT MARS IN HISTORY. GRS discovered vast deposits of buried subsurface hydrogen/water ice beneath 1 meter of soil across high latitudes; THEMIS mapped global thermal inertia.
payload: THEMIS (Thermal Emission Imaging System - 9 IR & 5 Vis bands)
GRS (Gamma Ray Spectrometer Suite: Gamma Sensor, Neutron Spectrometer, HEND)

objectives: High-resolution 3D color stereo imaging, mineralogical mapping, subsurface radar sounding, atmospheric tracing.
key_discoveries: Discovered hydrated phyllosilicate clays in ancient terrains (proving Noachian neutral-pH water); MARSIS detected dielectric anomalies interpreted as subglacial liquid brine pools beneath South Polar Layered Deposits.
payload: OMEGA (Visible and Infrared Mineralogical Mapping Spectrometer)

objectives: Search for geological evidence of past liquid water activity in Gusev Crater.
key_discoveries: Traveled 7.73 km; scaled Columbia Hills (Husband Hill summit); jammed right-front wheel dragged trench at 'Home Plate' revealing 90% pure opal-like silica formed by ancient hydrothermal fumaroles/hot springs.

objectives: Investigate hematite-rich plain of Meridiani Planum for evidence of past aqueous environments.
key_discoveries: RECORD HOLDER FOR LONGEST DRIVING DISTANCE OFF EARTH (45.16 km over 14.5 years). Hole-in-one landing in Eagle Crater; discovered hematite spherules ('blueberries') and jarosite sulfate cross-bedding formed in ancient acidic playa lakes.
payload: Full MER Instrumental Suite identical to Spirit (Pancam, Mini-TES, Mössbauer, APXS, RAT, Microscopic Imager)

objectives: Ultra-high resolution surface imaging (30 cm/pixel), atmospheric profiling, shallow subsurface radar sounding.
key_discoveries: HiRISE imaged active avalanche plumes, rover hardware, Recurring Slope Lineae (RSL), fresh impact craters; SHARAD detected massive buried water-ice sheets under lobate debris aprons in mid-latitudes; returned >450 terabits of science data.
payload: HiRISE (High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment - 50 cm aperture)
CRISM (Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars)

objectives: Excavate permafrost soil and subsurface ice in arctic plains of Vastitas Borealis; assess habitability.
key_discoveries: DIRECT DETECTION OF WATER ICE ON MARS SURFACE: trench showed white ice chunks that sublimated over 4 days; TEGA melted ice confirming H2O; wet chemistry cell discovered magnesium perchlorate (ClO4-) acting as antifreeze.

objectives: Assess whether Gale Crater ever had environmental conditions favorable for microbial life; investigate organic chemistry.
key_discoveries: PROVED ANCIENT MARS HAD A HABITABLE FRESHWATER LAKE SYSTEM (Yellowknife Bay, mudstones containing C, H, N, O, P, S). Discovered indigenous organic carbon molecules (thiophenes, alkyls) in 3.5 Ga lacustrine mudstone; detected seasonal background methane cycle and spikes; climbed >800 m up Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons).
payload: SAM (Sample Analysis at Mars - Quadrupole Mass Spec, GC, Tunable Laser Spectrometer)

objectives: Determine rate of atmospheric loss to space today and extrapolate total atmospheric escape over Mars history.
key_discoveries: Measured solar wind stripping ions at ~100 grams/second during solar storms; demonstrated that unshielded solar stripping transformed Mars from warm/wet early planet into current arid desert.
payload: NGIMS (Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer)

objectives: Investigate internal structure of Mars (crust, mantle, core) using seismology, precision geodesy, and heat flow.
key_discoveries: FIRST SEISMIC OBSERVATORY ON MARS: detected 1,319 marsquakes (up to magnitude 4.7); mapped crustal thickness (24-72 km); determined large liquid core radius (~1,830 km) and enriched light-element sulfur core composition.
payload: SEIS (Seismic Experiment for Interior Structure / CNES)
HP3 (Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package 'Mole' / DLR)
APSS (Auxiliary Payload Sensor Suite - Wind, Temp, Pressure)

objectives: Perform comprehensive orbital remote sensing and surface in-situ exploration in Utopia Planitia.
key_discoveries: China became the second nation to successfully operate a rover on Mars. Zhurong rover traversed 1,921 m; RoPeR ground-penetrating radar discovered buried multi-layered sedimentary structures and hydrated minerals in southern Utopia Planitia.
payload: Tianwen-1 Orbiter: High-Res Camera (HiRIC), Moderate-Res Camera (MoRIC), Mars Subsurface Radar (MOSIR)
Zhurong Rover: Multispectral Camera (MSCam), Mars Surface Composition Detector (MarSCoDe), Subsurface Radar (RoPeR), Surface Magnetic Field Detector (RoMS), Mars Climate Station (MCS)

mission_type: Mars Astrobiology Rover, Sample Caching & Aerial Scout
objectives: Seek signs of ancient microbial life in Jezero Crater paleolake and delta; core and cache pristine rock samples for Earth return; demonstrate powered flight in thin atmosphere.
key_discoveries: INGENUITY PERFORMED FIRST POWERED CONTROLLED FLIGHT ON ANOTHER PLANET (72 flights, 128 minutes aloft, 17 km flown). Perseverance drilled and sealed 24+ core samples; MOXIE successfully produced oxygen from atmospheric CO2; SHERLOC and PIXL detected diverse organic macromolecules associated with sulfate and carbonate minerals in the river delta.
